I'm a graduate researcher in the Genetics, Genomics and Systems Biology ([GGSB](https://ggsb.uchicago.edu/)) program at The University of Chicago, where I work under [Haky Im]({{< var site.hrefs.imlab >}}). Before this, I completed a master's at The University of North Dakota, supervised by [Junguk Hur](https://med.und.edu/labs/hur/).

I work at the intersection of machine learning, genomics, and analyzing clinical data. In my doctoral work, I developed genetic predictors of molecular phenotypes using sequence-to-function models, and tested their association with diseases. 

I have done this successfully for transcription factor binding. We called the framework [TFXcan](https://github.com/hakyimlab/TFXcan), and it helps us to better understand what TFs are driving a phenotype. 

We have also applied this idea to develop genetic predictors of pediatric phenotypes, work that contributed to the [developmental GTEx project](https://gtexportal.org/home/aboutDGtex), and showed that we can find more disease-relevant genes if we use the right contexts. 

Other works that I have done, including on drug-induced liver injury, postpartum depression, and cell segmentation can be found in my [publications](content/assets/publications/index.qmd) page. 

You can also check out my [blog](content/blog/index.qmd) to see what I am up to. 

## Outside work

I like to volunteer in food pantries, sing, play pick up soccer, do Origami, play the guitar, see live theatre, choral and orchestral performances. I also have a [GoodReads]({{< var site.hrefs.goodreads >}}) reading list.
